newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris urges peaceful settlement of Comoros crisis.
newsitem.headline: Paris urges peaceful settlement of Comoros crisis.

text.p: France again urged a peaceful settlement of the separatist crisis in the Comoros on Monday as a mediator from the Organisation of African Unity arrived on the Indian Ocean island group for negotiations.

"France urges the federal authorities and all Comoran political factions to unite in their efforts, under the OAU's guidance, to find a consensual solution which respects the aspirations of all Comorans," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
France has refused to back the separatist revolt on two of the three islands in the Comoros archipelago, which became independent from France in 1975.

The two islands, Anjouan and Moheli, have announced they are breaking away from Comoros, angered by their islands' poverty and the relative prosperity of the nearby island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains French.
Secessionists say that the main island of Grand Comore has been favoured over the other two islands.

The OAU said last week that envoy Pierre Yere of Ivory Coast would discuss measures to defuse tension "while addressing the legitimate concerns of the islanders while maintaining the unity, territorial integrity and cohesion of Comoros."
